The Delta County Sherriff's Department reported two structures fires and a tree fire in Escanaba as a result of lightning strikes.  It took over three and a half hours for firefighters to extinguish the first fire which occurred in the attic of a house at 514 South 12th Street.  A man and his dog were rescued from one of the apartments at this residence.  Fire fighter fatigue was reported to be a major difficulty at this fire due to the heat and humidity, and one firefighter sustained a minor injury while fighting the blaze.  Escanaba Public Safety was assisted on the scene by Delta County Central Dispatch, the Escanaba Township and Ford River Township fire departments, Gladstone Public Safety Volunteer Fire Fighters, MSP 84, the Delta County Sheriff's Department, Rampart EMS, DTE, Escanaba City Electric and the Red Cross.  ||While responding to the fire on South 12th Street, firefighters had to extinguish a tree fire and a second structure fire at an abandoned residence on 1612 North 20th Street.

A microburst struck Indian River Campground southeast of Steuben in Schoolcraft County on the afternoon of the 14th. Over 50 large trees were snapped or uprooted over a 300 x 200 yard area. Maximum wind speeds were estimated at 85 mph. Fortunately, all of the campsites were empty at the time of the storm.

Extensive straight-line wind damage was found in and around the town of Marenisco with estimated wind speeds up to 90 mph.  Some structural damage was found, but most of the damage was uprooted or snapped trees.  The main structural damage was significant roof damage to a newly-built garage at the corner of Hall and Mill Streets in Marenisco where over a quarter of the metal roof and decking was stripped back and torn from the roof trusses.  A continuous swath of straight-line wind damage started approximately five miles west of town to six miles southeast of town and continued into the Ottawa National Forest.  Campers were trapped at Bobcat Lake Campground due to fallen trees, but no injuries were reported.  Many roads were closed due to fallen trees in the area, and numerous power outages were reported. The time of the report was estimated from radar.

Lightning sparked a wildfire on Isle Royale. The fire began August 10, 2021. The Horne Fire in a remote area of Isle Royale National Park near the shore of Duncan Bay by the Tobin-Duncan Portage burned approximately 521 acres by the end of August. The fire continued to slowly burn and smolder into September with the Park Service awaiting the arrival of snow to fully extinguish the fire.

events.event_narrative: The Minneapolis Shoal Light station measured northwest storm force wind gusts to 56 mph.

Snowfall reports over an approximate 16-hour period included 14.4 inches at Spalding, 12 inches at Daggett and 11 inches at Stephenson.  East to northeast gusting near 35 mph at times during the event also caused drifting of snow and greatly reduced visibility in snow and blowing snow. Power outages were reported across portions of Menominee County from the storm.

Snowfall reports over less than a 24-hour period included anywhere from 10 to 14 inches in the Escanaba-Gladstone area, near 11 inches at Bark River and 16 inches at Garden Corners. The heavy snowfall combined with northwest winds gusting over 30 mph caused widespread power outages throughout Delta County on the 11th.

Snowfall reports over an approximate 16-hour period included 14 inches near Dollarville and 12 to 14 inches in the Newberry area. The heavy snowfall combined with north winds gusting to 35 mph at times caused power outages over portions of the county.

Snowfall reports over an approximate 18-hour time period ranged from 12 to 18 inches inches near Manistique to around 13 inches at Cooks near the Delta-Schoolcraft county line. The combination of the heavy snowfall and north winds gusting to 35 mph at times caused power outages over portions of Schoolcraft County.
Snowfall estimates ranges from 10 to 14 inches across northern Schoolcraft County during the event.

Snowfall reports across an approximate 10-hour period ending at 8 am on the 11th included 10 inches southwest of Munising and 10 inches near Forest Lake.  Grand Marais measured a storm total of 12 inches of snow over an 18-hour period. Additional snow falling into the early afternoon along with north winds gusting to 50 mph at times caused near blizzard conditions at times on the 11th.

Snowfall amounts over an approximate 16-hour period ranged from 5 inches in Marquette to 8 to 12 inches away from the Lake Superior shoreline.  North winds gusting over 40 mph caused near blizzard conditions at times on the morning of the 11th.

The Marquette County Police/Fire Dispatch reported widespread tree and power line damage from Negaunee through Marquette to Harvey and Gwinn on the morning of the 16th.  One tree fell on a mobile home at 553 Mobile Estates near Gwinn.  Many roads were partially or totally blocked from downed trees.  The Marquette Board of Light and Power reported that outages reached up to 1,000 in Marquette, Negaunee, Harvey and surrounding areas, and UPPCO reported nearly 6000 customers without power between Marquette and Iron counties from the storm. Republic-Michigamme Schools were also closed on the 16th.
There was a report from a school bus driver relayed through police dispatch of a power line down across Powell Lake Road south of Wetmore.
A large tree fell on a house just southwest of Escanaba and caused minor cuts and bruises to a person in the house at the time.  House damage included a hole in the roof and smashed windows.
There was a report through Facebook of a 10-inch diameter tree down in a yard off Leeman Road in Sagola.

Extensive tree and power line damages was reported throughout northern Houghton on the morning of the 16th with numerous reports of trees blocking roads and a few reports of trees down on unoccupied cars.  There was a report of a tree down on a house on Pine Street in Lake Linden.  Houghton-Keweenaw Schools were closed on the 16th, and Houghton and Keweenaw counties combined reported more than 2000 customers without power from the storm.

There were reports of power lines down and trees down across roads in the Eagle Harbor area.  Houghton-Keweenaw Schools were closed on the 16th due to the wind storm and more than 2000 customers were without power over Keweenaw and Houghton counties combined.
High winds knocked the power out to several thousand customers in Iron County or more than 60 percent of the customers tracked by UPPCO and Wisconsin Electric.
A spotter near Swanson reported lots of branches down from a small old maple tree.

Moderate to occasionally heavy lake effect snow of 4 to 5 inches was reported from Big Bay through Negaunee and Marquette to Harvey during the afternoon and evening of the 23rd.  ||The moderate to heavy snow likely contributed to a fatal accident on Highway M-553 just north of Marquette Mountain.  Police say a Ford Fusion, driven by a 70-year-old Marquette man, was traveling north on M-553 at 729 pm when the driver lost control and crossed the center line.  The Ford Fusion collided with a Nissan Versa driven by a 65-year-old Marquette man.  There were two passengers in the Ford and one in the Nissan.  All five people were transported to UPHS-Marquette for treatment.  The passenger of the Nissan, a 63-year-old Marquette woman, was pronouned dead at the hospital.  The crash shut down M-553 for hours between Division Street and County Road 480.
